items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to authorizing the New
York state energy research and development authority to develop a clean energy
outreach and community planning program; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon the expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Add Art 8 Title 9-C §§1910 - 1914, Pub Auth L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2956

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to authorizing
the New York state energy research and development authority to develop
a clean energy outreach and community planning program; and providing
for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:

This bill would authorize the New York State Energy Research and Devel-
opment Authority (NYSERDA) to develop a Clean Energy Outreach and Commu-
nity Planning Program with an emphasis on outreach and education on how
to maximize the benefits of renewable energy projects while minimizing
community impacts and the development of new renewable energy siting and
planning resources, including a Clean Energy Development Mapping Tool,
to support the appropriate and successful siting of renewable energy
projects, including wind, solar, storage and transmission and distrib-
ution system upgrades.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

§ 1- Amends Article 8 of the Public Authorities Law by adding a new
Title 9-C, the Clean Energy Outreach and Community Planning Program.

§ 1910-Statement of legislative finding and intent. New York will need
to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy projects in order to
achieve the mandates of the New York State Climate Leadership and Commu-
nity Protection Act (CLCPA). This acceleration can only be achieved
through a multi-pronged approach to provide communities, including
disadvantaged communities as designated under the CLCPA, with the infor-
mation, tools and funding necessary to support the appropriate siting
and community acceptance of renewable energy sources, including wind,
solar, storage and transmission and distribution upgrades by host commu-
nities. This requires the establishment of programs and mechanisms to
educate the public, build consensus and equip local governments with the
tools and funding they need to effectively consider and determine their
land use, including local planning and zoning.

§ 1911-Definitions. Provides for the definition of, "Authority",
"Departments", "Disadvantaged communities" and "Renewable energy facili-
ty".

§ 1912-Powers and duties. NYSERDA is authorized to establish a Clean
Energy Outreach and Community Planning Program to provide information,
resources and funding to support local communities in their land use
decisions and support the appropriate and successful siting of renewable
energy facilities. This includes developing a community education and
engagement program to inform New Yorkers about the climate crisis, the
benefits of shifting to a clean energy economy and conducting outreach,
including to local governments, and the facilitation of regional
discussions and forums to provide information and education on maximiz-
ing the benefits that renewable energy projects can provide while mini-
mizing community impacts.

In addition, NYSERDA is authorized and directed to collaborate with
community stakeholders, the agriculture and forestry sectors, the renew-
able energy industry, and utilities to develop new renewable energy
planning tools and resources for local governments. Such resources shall
include a Clean Energy Development Mapping Tool to help municipal repre-
sentatives and local communities make informed land use decisions and
communicate local priorities to developers and technical assistance and
training to local governments and other stakeholders on the use of such
tools and resources. The Clean Energy Development Mapping Tool should be
designed to facilitate participation by local governments, renewable
energy developers, and others in existing renewable energy siting and
planning processes and programs administered by NYSERDA and the Public
Service Commission, including NY-Sun, Large-Scale Renewables solicita-
tions and the Coordinated Grid Planning Process.

§ 1913-Funding. NYSERDA may seek funding from any authorized or other
available source to administer the Clean Energy Outreach and Community
Planning Program.

§ 1914-Reporting. NYSERDA shall Issue an annual report regarding the
effectiveness of the program and providing recommendations for improve-
ments to the program starting April 1, 2023. This report shall include:
(a) the number and identity of communities and local governments reached
through the comprehensive education, engagement and outreach effort; (b)
the number of regional discussion forums held for communities and devel-
opers, and identification of attendees and description of outcomes; (c)
the number, description and status of renewable energy planning tools
and resources developed, including the clean energy development mapping
tool; (d) the number and identity of local governments receiving techni-
cal assistance and training on the clean energy mapping tool and other
resources; (e) the number of service providers and contracts awarded;
(f) the amount of funds invested in the clean energy outreach and commu-
nity planning program; and (g) any additional information relevant to
assessing program effectiveness.

§ 2-Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The goals of the New York State Climate Leadership and Community
Protection Act (CLCPA) will only be met if New York accelerates the
deployment of renewable energy projects. This acceleration can only be
achieved through a multi-pronged approach to provide communities,
including disadvantaged communities, with the information, tools,
including a Clean Energy Development Mapping Tool, and funding necessary
to support the appropriate and successful siting of renewable energy
sources. This requires the establishment of programs and mechanisms to
educate the public, build consensus and equip local governments with the
tools and funding they need to effectively consider and determine their
land use, including local planning and zoning.

The CLCPA enacted in 2019, was pioneering legislation that took serious-
ly the climate challenges faced by our planet. In its very name it prom-
ised equity between climate-smart advances and protecting the values of
our local communities in this Home Rule state. It suggests, as well, a
balance between the scale and placement of renewable energy developments
and the protection of local communities, including their health, econo-
my, and culture, whether rural or urban.


The challenges of this balancing act have been playing out over the last
several years across the state. While some communities have welcomed
these solar projects and have developers who work cooperatively with the
host community, it is dear that not all developers are so accommodating.
Some communities are concerned about their rights and protections as
host communities to both small-scale and large-scale renewable energy
projects and often express that the scales have been tipped to benefit
developers, many of which are not based in New York, including those who
intend to quickly sell their solar sites, leaving local communities with
no voice and no long-term safeguards.

The multi-pronged approach envisioned in this legislation to provide for
outreach, education, tools and resources to allow local governments and
communities to understand the climate crisis, the renewable energy
projects available, the benefits of shifting to a dean energy economy,
make informed land use decisions, and communicate local priorities to
developers is vital as New York State strives to meet our climate goals.
GISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Yet to be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire December 31,
2030 when upon such date this act shall be deemed repealed.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 81 Chapter 759
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2956-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the public authorities law and the executive law,
        in relation to authorizing the New York  state  energy  research
        and development authority to develop a clean energy outreach and
        community planning program; and providing for the repeal of such
        provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  authorize  and  direct  the  New  York State Energy
Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) to establish a clean energy
outreach and community planning program. It further would require NYSER-
DA to develop a mapping tool which would provide information  and  guid-
ance  to  communities  for evaluation of potential clean energy projects
and require NYSERDA to issue an annual report regarding  the  effective-
ness and provide recommendations for improvements.
 
  I  support  the  goals  of  this  bill, which would increase community
outreach for renewable energy projects. However, as drafted,  this  bill
would  require  NYSERDA  to  expend  resources on creating a new program
instead of building on its existing outreach programs. NYSERDA currently
has a Clean Energy Siting team serving similar functions and the  bill's
language  should  reflect  the  expansion of existing programming. Addi-
tionally, NYSERDA is currently  developing  an  Integrated  Energy  Data
Resource  platform that can obtain data to meet the criteria required in
the legislation for the mapping tool. Changes to this bill  were  neces-
sary  to  ensure  its  requirements align with and expand upon NYSERDA's
existing programs.

  I have reached an agreement with the Legislature to enact these chang-
es.  On the basis of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
